source_name: Racunovodstvo.net – free consolidated texts of ZPlaSSIED and banking statutes (article-level)
why_relevant: Free, article-by-article republication of the Slovenian Payment Services, E-Money Issuance and Payment Systems Act (ZPlaSSIED) — the national transposition of PSD2. Useful as an accessible, linkable mirror and terminology source, but secondary: always confirm against PISRS/Uradni list.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Archive of former publications
why_relevant: The supervisor's own archive of discontinued publication series — the first place to look for superseded financial stability reports, supervisory statistics and reporting notices that no longer appear in the current publications navigation.

source_name: Banka Slovenije statistical data warehouse (PxWeb 'Podatkovne serije')
why_relevant: Machine-queryable time-series database behind the central bank's statistical releases (financial markets, banking sector). PxWeb gives stable series identifiers and export formats, making it the statistical-release layer of this cell rather than a PDF-scraping problem.

source_name: European e-Justice Portal – National legislation: Slovenia
why_relevant: EU-maintained English-language description of the Slovenian legal-information architecture (PIS, its ~15 integrated databases, Uradni list as gazette of record, language coverage). Best onboarding map of which Slovenian database holds what, and a stable pointer when national portals are restructured.

source_name: EU representation in Slovenia – transposition news (Predstavništvo EK v Sloveniji)
why_relevant: Slovenian-language Commission communications about transposition of EU legislation into national law, including infringement-package announcements naming Slovenia. A translation layer that surfaces EU enforcement pressure in the local language and vocabulary.

source_name: Third-party regulatory transposition trackers (ECSO NIS2 tracker, law-firm CSRD/NIS2 trackers)
why_relevant: Pattern-establishing example of privately maintained per-Member-State transposition trackers that state Slovenia's status and national instrument for a given directive, often faster than official notification. Relevant for banking-adjacent files (NIS2, DORA interplay, CSRD) where bank compliance deadlines are affected. Treat as a lead, verify against PISRS/EUR-Lex.

source_name: PISRS - Pravno-informacijski sistem Republike Slovenije (official publication platform for Uradni list RS since 1 March 2026)
source_subtype: official legislation register / official gazette platform
why_relevant: PISRS is the consolidated legislation register of Slovenia and, per a transition notice on uradni-list.si citing Art. 33 ZoUL, has taken over official publication of the Uradni list RS as of 1 March 2026. It carries the legally authoritative text, publication date, entry-into-force and transposition dates for ZBan, ZPlaSSIED and ZPPDFT and all their novele. This is the single hardest-dated primary channel for the cell.

source_name: UL info tok / Uradni list e-bilten (legislative-change notification service)
why_relevant: The gazette publisher's own alerting layer: 'obveščanje o zakonodajnih novostih', newsletter and e-bilten news items that editorially flag what changed and when it applies. Useful as a low-cost tripwire that a new banking/AML/payments act has been published, and its plain-language notes explain effect dates.

source_name: Državni zbor RS - Prečiščena besedila zakonov (parliament-issued consolidated texts)
why_relevant: Parliament publishes official consolidated texts (UPB) after amendment waves. The appearance of a new ZBan or ZPlaSSIED UPB is itself a signal that the amendment cycle has closed, and gives a clean single text to diff against the prior consolidation.

source_name: Ministrstvo za finance (GOV.SI) - news RSS and ministry pages
why_relevant: The sponsoring ministry for ZBan, ZPlaSSIED and (with the Office for Money Laundering Prevention) ZPPDFT. Its GOV.SI news RSS (orgID 24) announces the opening of public consultations, adoption of bills by the government, and outcome summaries of consultations - e.g. the 7 Apr 2025 announcement of a draft-law consultation and the list of respondents (Banka Slovenije, ZBS, KPK, ANR, GZS, Informacijski pooblaščenec). A ready-made RSS feed is a rare gift in this landscape.

source_name: Državni svet RS (National Council) - sessions, opinions and suspensive veto
why_relevant: The second chamber can impose a suspensive veto (odložilni veto) that forces a re-vote in the National Assembly and pushes entry-into-force back by weeks. It has done so on banking legislation before (the 2013 banking act and the 2019 act on judicial protection of former holders of qualified bank liabilities). Its committee opinions carry EPA numbers, letting them be joined to the DZ pipeline. This is the main source of schedule risk that a gazette-only feed would miss.

source_name: Banka Slovenije - Plačilne storitve in storitve izdajanja elektronskega denarja (supervisor's legal-basis page)
why_relevant: The competent authority's own restatement of the ZPlaSSIED legal framework and the subordinate acts (sklepi) it issues under it. Useful as a cross-check on which version of the statute is operative and as the bridge from primary law to supervisory implementing acts, which are themselves published in the gazette. Adjacent to another coverage cell but load-bearing for confirming statutory citations.

source_name: Računovodstvo.net - zakonodaja / časovnica predpisov
why_relevant: Free practitioner-oriented mirror that maintains a per-act timeline (e.g. a single page tracking ZPPDFT, ZPPDFT-1 and ZPPDFT-2 together). Cheap, open, and good for quickly establishing the amendment lineage of an act before going to the authoritative register. Secondary - verify every date against the gazette.

source_name: Zakonodaja.com - article-level statute browser
why_relevant: Free site exposing Slovenian statutes at individual-article granularity with NPB (neuradno prečiščeno besedilo) version labels - useful when the question is 'what exactly changed in article X of the payments act'. Unofficial consolidations, so treat as a navigation aid only.

source_name: FinD-INFO / IUS-INFO medijsko središče (LEXPERA legal-news wire)
why_relevant: Daily curated legal/financial news selection from the dominant Slovenian legal publisher. It reliably reports bills entering parliament and statutes entering into force before the analyst would spot them in the gazette, and it names the practitioners commenting on them - a useful actor-discovery surface for snowballing.

source_name: N-Lex - Slovenian national law collection (EU access point)
why_relevant: The European Commission's documented gateway into each member state's national legal database, including a description page for the Slovenian collection. Valuable as an independent, English-language description of which Slovenian database is authoritative and how it is queried - exactly the kind of pointer that stays correct across the 2026 Uradni list to PISRS migration.

source_name: OPSI - Odprti podatki Slovenije (national open data portal, CKAN)
why_relevant: The portal that reveals which Slovenian institutions publish machine-readable feeds at all. It already yielded the DZ bills XML and a PISRS 'Osnovni podatki o predpisih RS / Zbirke PISRS' dataset. Running its CKAN search over the local-language glossary is the cheapest way to find further structured legislative feeds instead of scraping portals.

source_name: PISRS dataset on OPSI: Osnovni podatki o predpisih RS / Zbirke PISRS
why_relevant: The open-data manifestation of the legislation register - basic metadata for all Slovenian regulations, including collections such as invalid/lapsed regulations and acts whose adoption procedure ended without adoption. That negative set is unusually valuable: it tells you which draft banking or payments acts died, which a gazette-only feed can never show.

source_name: Uradni list RS English-language and EU-facing act pages (en secondary channel)
why_relevant: English coverage of Slovenian primary banking legislation is thin and non-authoritative - the gazette publishes in Slovene. Tracked here only to record that the English route exists mainly through supervisor translations (Banka Slovenije en pages) and EU-level transposition notices, not through the gazette itself. Important for setting expectations on en-language collection.

source_name: EBA — Consultation papers (all open/closed consultations, with response deadlines)
why_relevant: Primary EU-level origin of binding technical standards and guidelines that Banka Slovenije and SI banks/PSPs must apply. Each paper carries an explicit response deadline and public-hearing date, giving 3-12 months of lead time before Slovenian applicability.

source_name: EBA — Interactive Single Rulebook / Regulation and policy hub
why_relevant: Canonical index mapping Level 1 EU acts to the RTS/ITS/Guidelines under them, with application dates. Best single pointer for enumerating what will bind Slovenian institutions and when.

source_name: EBA — Guidelines compliance tables (national competent authority 'comply or explain', incl. Banka Slovenije)
why_relevant: The compliance table attached to each EBA guideline states explicitly whether Banka Slovenije complies, intends to comply (with date), or does not — the single most direct evidence of Slovenian applicability of an EU-level soft-law instrument.

source_name: EBA — Opinions and Reports (incl. transition-period opinions)
why_relevant: EBA Opinions frequently set or clarify supervisory expectations and end-dates (e.g. Opinion EBA/OP/2026/01 on the end of the NAL transition period) that NCAs including Banka Slovenije then apply.

source_name: EBA — Credit institutions / payment institutions registers (EUCLID-based public registers)
why_relevant: Pan-EU register listing authorised credit institutions and PSD2 payment/e-money institutions per Member State, including SI entities and passporting into Slovenia. Structural map of who is in scope of the rules.

source_name: ECB Banking Supervision — List of supervised entities (SI / LSI, monthly PDF + data)
why_relevant: Authoritative determination of which Slovenian banks are ECB-supervised significant institutions (NLB Group; Gorenjska Banka via AikGroup; OTP's SI operations via OTP Luxembourg) versus LSIs left to Banka Slovenije. Directly defines the SI-designated-significant perimeter for this cell.

source_name: ECB Banking Supervision — SSM supervisory priorities and risk assessment
why_relevant: Annual multi-year priorities set the examination and thematic-review agenda that flows down to SI-designated significant institutions and, via Banka Slovenije, to LSIs. Strong leading indicator of where supervisory pressure (and vendor demand) will land.

source_name: ECB Banking Supervision — Public consultations (guides, ECB Regulations, options and discretions)
why_relevant: ECB consultations on supervisory guides and ECB Regulations carry hard response deadlines and later become directly applicable to SI-designated significant institutions without national transposition.
